title: Roadmap: Go is the next LanguageSpec registry entry; Dart deferred pending demand
context: Charter rejected breadth-first, not breadth-ever (dec_36a4c9cff8); Python already proved the registry path. Hunch's memory core (decisions, bugs, constraints, corrections) is language-agnostic — grammar breadth only widens the structure tools (symbols, blast radius, conformance), so a Go-repo user already gets most of Hunch today; a grammar closes the rest. Go is the strongest candidate: mature official tree-sitter grammar with good prebuild coverage, a simple unambiguous import model (package paths), and a large agentic-coding audience. The real per-language cost is not the registry entry but the native prebuild matrix (Node ABI x 3 platforms), install weight (each grammar is a native dep — consider optional-dep packaging so non-users skip the download), per-language import-resolution semantics, builtin-method lists, and a test corpus.
decision: Add Go as the next supported language via the LanguageSpec registry (one registry entry + tree-sitter-go grammar dep), when demand shows. Dart is explicitly deferred until a real demand signal (Flutter users asking) AND a grammar-quality check passes. Any added grammar must honor the dec_36a4c9cff8 guardrails: prebuilds for win32/linux/darwin riding the per-process temp-copy loader (EBUSY class stays dead), Constitution mutation controls / behavior evaluators remain TS-scoped (indexing breadth is not evaluator breadth), and import resolution keeps the don't-guess-on-ambiguity rule.
consequences: Go grammar must ship win32/linux/darwin prebuilds and ride the per-process temp-copy loader before landing
Evaluator/Constitution scope stays TS until separately proven — adding Go touches indexing only
Install weight grows with each grammar; evaluate optional-dep packaging before the second added language
Rust/Java rank ahead of Dart if demand appears for either
alternatives_rejected: Dart next: community-maintained grammar, less mature, spottier prebuild coverage, and no demand signal yet — deferred (not rejected forever), revisit when Flutter users ask and the grammar passes a quality check

Breadth blitz (Go+Dart+Rust+Java at once): violates the breadth-after-core discipline; each grammar multiplies the prebuild maintenance matrix and install weight — add one language at a time, on demand
Stay TS/JS+Python forever: the charter's rejection was of breadth-first, not breadth-ever; the registry design already paid the setup cost and Go demand among agentic-coding users is high
